lines.text: Date of service: 02/03/2026 Arrival: 14:32 MRN: BRM-4471902
Neck pain and low back pain after a motor vehicle collision.
37-year-old female, restrained driver, rear-ended at a stop light at moderate speed about one hour
before arrival. Airbags did not deploy. Reports immediate neck stiffness and low back pain, pain 7/10.
Denies loss of consciousness, numbness or weakness.
Tenderness over the cervical paraspinal muscles and the lumbar paraspinal muscles. Range of motion
of the neck reduced by pain. Strength 5/5 in all extremities. Sensation intact.
CT head without contrast: no acute intracranial abnormality.
X-ray cervical spine, 3 views: no fracture or malalignment.
Ketorolac 30 mg IM given at 15:10. Pain improved to 5/10.
1. S13.4XXA - Sprain of ligaments of cervical spine, initial encounter
2. S33.5XXA - Sprain of ligaments of lumbar spine, initial encounter

findings.title: Duplicate document left out of the totals
findings.detail: Emergency department bill (faxed copy) is a copy of Emergency department bill (identical letter for letter, after OCR). Counting both would overstate the bills.

findings.title: Bill total does not match its line items
findings.detail: Pacific Spine & Orthopedics prints a total of $3,215.00, but its 4 charges add up to $3,115.00 (a difference of $100.00). Exhibit uses the line items.

findings.title: Charge with no treatment note
findings.detail: Harbor Physical Therapy bills $245.00 for Mar 23, 2026, but no record in the file documents a visit that day. Request the note, or expect the charge to be challenged.

findings.title: 33-day gap in treatment
findings.detail: No documented care between Mar 19, 2026 (Harbor Physical Therapy) and Apr 21, 2026 (Pacific Spine & Orthopedics). Insurers use gaps over 30 days to argue the injury had resolved; the reason for the gap should be documented.
